probability_status.description: Why `combined_probability` is or is not there, as a fixed value a client can map to its own wording. `computed`: every active leg had a `win_probability` and the active legs are from distinct known events, so the probabilities were multiplied (assumes independence). A single active leg has nothing to be correlated with, so it counts as distinct with or without an `event_id`. `needs_leg_probabilities`: the same holds for the events, but at least one active leg has no `win_probability`. `same_event_legs`: two or more active legs share an `event_id`, so their results are correlated. `unverified_legs`: there are several active legs and at least one has no `event_id`, so independence cannot be checked. `no_active_legs`: every leg pushed or was voided. `combined_probability` is a number only for `computed` and null for every other value. Precedence when several apply: `no_active_legs`, then `same_event_legs`, then `unverified_legs`, then `needs_leg_probabilities`, then `computed`.

info.description:
OddVex is a sports-betting **intelligence** API: odds comparison, player-prop research,
betting math and bet tracking. It never accepts, places or facilitates wagers.

**By default all sports data served by this build is synthetic.** Teams, players,
sportsbooks, prices and statistics are fictional and generated deterministically, and
responses carry `data_mode: "synthetic"`. An internal preview mode, `data_mode: "replay"`,
serves real past games shifted in time; its sportsbooks, prices and prop lines are simulated.

Conventions: JSON, snake_case, ISO-8601 UTC timestamps, string ids. Probabilities, holds, ROI
and CLV are fractions (0.05 = 5%) unless the field name ends in `_percent`. Errors use the
envelope `{"error": {"code", "message", "details"?}}`.
info.title: OddVex API

post.description:
For a data request from an owner who cannot sign in, and for closing an account that must not exist. Permanently deletes the user and everything `DELETE /v1/me` deletes, through the same code: bets, watchlist, alert rules, notifications and their preferences, the staking reminder, sync connections, import runs, email tokens, outbox emails and all community data. It cannot be undone. Works for an active and for a suspended account; when the account is suspended at that moment, its community handle stays reserved, so nobody can take it again.

`confirm_email` must be the account's email address (compared as login compares addresses), otherwise `422 confirm_email_mismatch` and nothing is deleted. `reason` is required and must not contain that address (`422 reason_contains_email`). The audit log keeps what the owner's own deletion keeps (the account's entries and an `account.deleted` entry, each with the opaque user id, the action, the id of the item acted on, the request id, the IP address and the details of the action) and an `admin.user_deleted` entry with the acting administrator, the user's id, the account's status and the reason; none holds the email address. An administrator cannot delete another administrator's account or their own (`409`). Answers `204` with no body.

post.description:
For a data request from an owner who cannot sign in: a suspended account, an account closed because its owner is under 21, a lost password. Returns the same document as `GET /v1/me/export` for that user, produced by the same code and streamed the same way: one JSON document without a `Content-Length`, to be read to the end and parsed once. It is the owner's data: pass it on to the owner only, and only once you know the request is theirs. Works for an active and for a suspended account and changes nothing in it.

`reason` is required and is recorded in the audit log as `admin.user_exported` with the acting administrator, the user's id and the account's status; the entry holds none of the exported data. The reason must not contain the account's email address (`422 reason_contains_email`). An administrator cannot export another administrator's account or their own (`409`); their own is at `GET /v1/me/export`. The response counts as one of the streamed responses the administrator can have in progress at the same moment (`ODDVEX_RATE_LIMIT_USER_STREAMS_AT_ONCE`): over it this answers `429 rate_limited`.

post.description:
Deterministic keyword routing to internal data tools with templated answers. No language model is connected and the assistant never produces a price, probability or amount that a tool did not compute. Authentication is optional; the bet summary intent needs it.

Before any routing, each message is checked against fixed patterns for crisis or self-harm language, for distress about gambling and for a user who says they are under 21. When one matches, the answer has intent `support`, carries help resources and no betting data, and `support.case` says which reply it is. A request for a certain winner gets a fixed answer with intent `fallback`. The patterns are a fixed list of rules and miss some messages, so every answer that is not a support reply ends with one sentence giving the gambling helpline and the crisis line.

post.description: Besides the per-IP limit, failed logins are counted per email address and client network (an IPv4 address, or the /64 prefix of an IPv6 address): after too many inside the window (8 in 15 minutes by default) further attempts for that email from that network get `429 rate_limited` until the window moves on, even with the right password. Attempts from other networks are not affected, so someone else's failures do not stop the owner from signing in. A second, higher ceiling counts the failures for one email from all networks together (50 in the same window by default); over it every attempt for that email gets the same `429`. Both apply whether or not an account exists for the email. A successful login clears the count of the caller's own network only. A suspended account gets `403 account_suspended` once the password is correct.

post.description:
OddVex never places wagers. This only records a bet for tracking. If you set a weekly staking reminder and this bet takes the week's total to or past it, a `stake_reminder` notification is created; the bet is saved either way.

The bet is checked completely before anything is saved. Prices are stored as decimal odds with six decimal places and stakes in cents: a price that would be stored as 1.000000 or less (`invalid_decimal_odds`), a price or combined parlay price above 9999999999.999999 (`odds_out_of_range`), a stake that would be stored as 0.00 (`invalid_stake`) and a stake and price whose payout is above 999999999999.99 (`payout_out_of_range`) are each a 422, and a 422 never saves anything.

**Retrying safely.** Send `client_request_id` (8 to 64 characters from `A-Z a-z 0-9 _ -`, for example a UUID made once per filled-in form) and send the same value again when you retry a create whose answer you did not receive. The first request stores the bet and answers 201. Every later request from the same account with the same id answers **200** with the bet that was stored the first time: no second bet, no second audit entry and no second staking reminder. The stored bet is returned even if the repeated body differs, so use a new id for a new or edited bet. This also holds when the retry arrives while the first request is still running. A repeat is still a request: a body that does not pass this schema is a 422 and a request over the write limit is a 429, with or without a known id. An id is only compared within one account, and is free again once that bet is deleted.

An account holds at most `ODDVEX_MAX_BETS_PER_USER` bets (default 5,000), imported bets included: at the cap this answers 409 `bet_limit_reached` with `details.max_bets`. Bet writes are limited per user (120 a minute and 2,000 a day by default): over the limit this answers 429 `rate_limited` with `Retry-After`.

200.description: A repeat of an earlier create with the same `client_request_id`: the bet stored the first time. Nothing new was saved

post.description: Looks at each of your pending bets. A bet is settled when every leg has a structured selection (`gradeable`) and every leg's event is final: the legs are graded from the final score and the bet goes through the same settlement as a manual settle, marked `settled_by: auto`. Other bets are listed in `skipped` with a reason. Calling this again settles nothing new. Each settled bet also creates a `bet_settled` notification. One call settles at most 200 bets, oldest first; when it stops there with pending bets left unexamined, `has_more` is true and calling again continues; it is false otherwise, and always sent. Counts towards the per-user write limit, and one account runs one auto-settle at a time: a call that arrives while another of the same account is still running is not started (both are 429 `rate_limited` with `Retry-After`).

get.description: `is_best` and `best` only consider books that are open and not stale. A quote is stale (`is_stale`) when it is older than `stale_after_seconds`, has no timestamp, carries a timestamp from the future, or, for a live event, was last updated before the latest score change. A stale quote is still listed but is never marked best and does not count in `consensus`. For spread and total, prices are only compared between books quoting the consensus (most common) line. `consensus` is the mean no-vig probability of those same books. One JSON document with your profile, bets, watchlist, alert rules, notifications, notification preferences, staking reminder, sync connections, import runs and your own audit entries, plus your community data (profile, picks, comments, who you follow, likes, blocks and reports you made). It never contains the password hash. The export itself is recorded in the audit log. A suspended account can still call this route.

The document is streamed: bets, import runs, audit entries and your community picks, comments and reports are read in batches and sent as they are read, so the response has no `Content-Length`. It is still one JSON document of this schema; read it to the end and parse it once. Limited per user (`ODDVEX_RATE_LIMIT_EXPORT_PER_HOUR`, default 10 an hour), and it counts as one of the streamed responses an account can have in progress at the same moment (`ODDVEX_RATE_LIMIT_USER_STREAMS_AT_ONCE`, default 8, shared with the bet list): over either limit this answers 429 `rate_limited` with `Retry-After`.

post.description:
Idempotent: bets are de-duplicated on provider + external bet id, so running this again never creates duplicates. Retryable provider errors are retried up to `ODDVEX_SYNC_MAX_ATTEMPTS` times. If the import still fails the run is recorded with status `failed` and this returns 502 with `details.run_id` and `details.retryable`. Either way a `sync_finished` notification is created, and imported bets count towards the weekly staking reminder.

Imported bets count against the same cap as `POST /v1/bets` (`ODDVEX_MAX_BETS_PER_USER`, default 5,000). The import takes the provider's bets in order and stops adding when the account is full; a bet whose price, stake or amount cannot be recorded is left out too. The run still succeeds and its `error_message` says how many bets were left out and why (the number is also `fetched_count - imported_count - duplicate_count`). Bets left out for room are offered again by a later import, once bets have been deleted. Counts towards the per-user write limit (429 `rate_limited` with `Retry-After`).

get.description: Outcomes of upcoming events whose best open, non-stale price is longer than the no-vig consensus of the other open, non-stale sportsbooks at the same line. Events in progress and finished events are never listed: in play, prices move with the score, so quotes taken moments apart are not comparable. The sportsbook with the best price is excluded from its own consensus and at least 2 other sportsbooks are required, otherwise the outcome is skipped. Sorted by `edge`, largest first. A price above the consensus is not proof of an edge and this is not a prediction; read `caveat`. `league` and `market` must be supported keys; any other value is a 422.
